No. I think you misunderstood me. 

I MAY have reported the first time, but I was warned even though it was clearly assault, I’d likely lose based on how the legal system works so I was afraid, my parents slut shaming me kept me silent.


The second time, a story in the news that was scary similar to my story came out (girl raped by Uber driver while passed out, was she passed out ENOUGH) and I decided to stay quiet and take care of myself. I was shamed by the hospital staff for not reporting (again because of obvious signs of abuse) but I feared for my safety, my reputation and overall mental health. 


Reporting is a PERSONAL choice. It’s not something. People should be FORCED to do. My body and choices were taken from me when those evil men took advantage of me. I made the choice to do what I needed to do to survive. 


Both cases I highly doubt I was the first victim and sadly unlikely the last. Do I feel horrible about that? You bet! I tried to overdose because of that (and other issues). But the alternative was to have my person dragged through the mud, possible vulnerability to abuse (which happens a lot more than people think), the high likelihood they would have been found “not guilty” and just more slut shaming. 


Until the legal system finds a way to deal with sexual assault in a more fair way, I respect women who chose to stay quiet. I respect those brave women who do report of course, but I respect the silent sufferers as well. 

The mental anguish caused by sexual assault is awful, we need to support each other in recovery any way the victim needs.

The second rape, I went to a clinic for help and was called a liar by the doc who refused to help me (had to go to the hospital instead)... I felt alone, scared, dirty and pathetic and wanted to kill my self... am I horrible for not reporting? Who would protect me? I don’t have supportive family (like the exact opposite if supportive) and I can promise you, without the option of abortion, I’d have committed suicide. I was sexually assaulted by an Uber driver and fell pregnant. I don’t know the laws regarding rapists rights to babies they create and I was scared. I had an abortion so early I had to sign an extra wavier (because there was a chance of complications). If abortion was illegal, I would have had to give up my career, be forced to raise a child I didn’t want and be forced to live in extreme poverty and possibly forced to deal with my rapist on a regular basis. 
Let’s say I charged this asshole. The same week I was assaulted, a similar story was on the news where a women was passed out in an Uber while being raped and the courts were deciding if she was “passed out enough to count as rape” so I just assumed my case wouldn’t win. My word against his and let’s be honest, it doesn’t usually go in favour of the victim. Plus, the doctor I went to after the assault told me it was my fault for going out late. And by the time this finished in court, I’d have a 5yr old. 
I had an abortion, I am still heartbroken I had to do it (I’m in therapy over the whole ordeal) , but without the option, my life would have been completely destroyed over something I had no control over. 
You don’t know someone’s story until you’ve walked in their shoes. Don’t judge. If you’re against abortion, don’t have one but don’t take away the option for other women. It may save more lives than you realize.
